Tessa / Procurement team — quick read-through from legal and proposed compromise items below.

1) Liability carveout: we can accept a limited carveout for GDPR data subject remediation only if Acme accepts a modified liability cap for those specific remedies. Suggested text in Section 9.3: "Redwood's liability for GDPR-related remediation for processed data shall be limited to direct remediation costs up to the lesser of USD X or the total fees paid in the prior 12 months."

2) Roles: keep processor designation in the Order Form but add a short mapping table (we put that in Exhibit B) that explicitly lists processing activities. That should address your compliance team's ask without changing the core model.

3) Subprocessor notification: 15-day notification for critical infra subprocessors is acceptable. For all others we keep 30 days, and we'll add an automatic publication feed for subprocessor changes (hosted page + email alert).

4) Evidence: procurement asked for SOC2 — we can provide the most recent SOC2 Type II report under NDA; if Acme needs additional encryption attestations (KMS/HSM) please specify and we'll include a short technical annex.

If Procurement is comfortable with the proposed language, I recommend Ben run CRO clearance on the liability carveout text this morning so we can issue a sign-off package for DocuSign.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Contracts | Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: SCCs-exhibit.pdf (prepared by legal)

From: Sara Linton <sara.linton@acmehealth.com>

Date: 2026-08-17T13:09:00-07:00

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the consolidated redline. A couple of clarifying asks from Acme legal before procurement can clear:

1) Liability cap language: Acme cannot accept a trimmed cap for GDPR remediation unless there is an explicit carveout for willful misconduct. Can Redwood confirm you will not remove willful misconduct from limitations?

2) Subprocessor notification: the 15-day window for critical infra is acceptable. We also need a 72-hour SLA for notification of any confirmed incident involving subprocessor infrastructure that impacts Acme customer data.

We will attach Acme's suggested edits (Acme_comments_v2.pdf). Once Redwood confirms the willful misconduct point and the incident notification SLA, Procurement will schedule final internal approval — after which we expect to route to your CRO for the narrow carveout approval. Can you provide SOC2 Type II evidence under NDA?

Regards,
Sara Linton
Senior Counsel, AcmeHealth
